To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bla TEM variants, bla TEM-116, bla TEM-190 and bla TEM-33 were found for the first time among Indian isolates and that bla TEM variants showed differential resistance pattern against β-lactam antibiotics.

bla TEM variants were detected in 57.8 % of E.coli and 50.5 % of K. pneumoniae isolates. bla TEM variants coexisted among 2.2% isolates. blaTEM-33 showed expanded activity towards β lactam-β-lac-tamase inhibitor combinations and differential resistance profile among the variants.
bla TEM-1, bla TEM-116, bla TEM-190 are the most common variants among pathogenic Enterobacteria infecting Indian patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first comprehensive molecular characterization of bla TEM variants in Enterobacteriacea isolates of Indian origin.
the molecular characterization of bla TEM variants and their resistance pattern among pathogenic enterobacteria of Indian origin, which is a first report.
the first report of TEM-33, TEM-116, and TEM-169 variants in India and their differential interaction with cephalospo-rins.

bla TEM variants are widely spread among Enterobactericeae in India, and bla TEM -33 and bla TEM -169 are novel variants.
bla TEM-33 is an emerging variant among Enterobacter species, and bla TEM variants are circulating in India, which can be considered as a public health concern.
bla TEM-1 and bla TEM-1-like variants are the most prevalent in India.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the TEM variants are prevalent among Enterobacteriacae in India and that their differential activity against cephalosporicins can be explained by their structural and intergenic relationships.
the bla TEM variants are circulating among Enterobacteriacae of Indian origin and are associated with resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
